summary: Cart implementation is broadly sound: parameterized SQL throughout, JWT-scoped user_id at every query, ON CONFLICT merge is tx-safe, no PII logged. Two MEDIUM correctness gaps (qty upper bound on update-item; UpdateItem(qty=0) breaks idempotent-remove contract) and one MEDIUM observability gap (inventory-down silent degrade) need fixing before L2. Stubs for remove-item / clear-on-checkout are tracked, not blocking at L1.
scope_checked: Auth: every endpoint extracts user_id from claims.sub; cart row filtered by user_id
Concurrent add-item ON CONFLICT path tx-safety

findings.title: cart.clear-on-checkout stubbed; AMB-002 customerUserId == claims.sub check must land before un-stubbing
findings.evidence: handler_clear_on_checkout.go:20-26 returns 501. router/router.go:68 wires the route under customer JWT only. TD AMB-002 requires customerUserId == claims.sub validation to prevent cross-customer leakage by a malicious checkout caller; absence of that check when the stub is replaced would be Cart-B-from-Customer-A class IDOR.
findings.impact: If implemented without claims.sub == customerUserId guard, a customer's token could clear another customer's cart items by passing a different customerUserId.
findings.recommendation: When implementing, validate customerUserId == claims.sub as step 1; reject with VALIDATION_ERROR on mismatch. Tag this as a P1 pre-merge check on the un-stub PR.

findings.title: Inventory bulk-read failure silently flips entire cart to checkoutable=false with no client-visible reason
findings.evidence: service.go:304-318 — on inventory error, stockMap is set to empty map and a slog.Warn fires. All items then get availableQty=0 (line 330) and checkoutable=false (line 332). subtotal becomes 0. Catalog-unreachable path (line 290-294) sets productStatus="CATALOG_UNREACHABLE" so clients can detect; no equivalent for inventory-unreachable.
findings.impact: Client cannot distinguish 'every item is OOS' from 'inventory service is down'. UX degrades to silent zero-stock cart; no retry signal.
findings.recommendation: Either (a) propagate UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT for the whole read on inventory failure (matching catalog-fail-fast path of cart.read failure_codes), or (b) add a per-line reason field (e.g. "inventory_unreachable") and a top-level cart-level inventoryStatus indicator.

findings.title: updateItemRequest.qty has no upper bound (only min=0)
findings.evidence: handler_update_item.go:19 — `Qty int json:"qty" binding:"min=0"`. addItemRequest at handler_add_item.go:18 correctly uses `min=1,max=100`. cart_items.qty column is INT (signed 32-bit).
findings.impact: A client can PATCH qty=2_147_483_647. Stock check usually rejects, but if inventory is unavailable or returns a high availableQty, the value persists. Downstream subtotal computation (service.go:333 `d.CurrentPrice * float64(item.Qty)`) can overflow expected business range and cause cosmetic / accounting noise. Reviewer guidance was 100/line.
findings.recommendation: Add `max=100` to updateItemRequest.Qty binding tag. Mirror the add-item validation.

findings.title: UpdateItem(qty=0) on already-removed line returns 404; direct RemoveItem returns gracefully — contract drift
findings.evidence: service.go:131-137 — UpdateItem calls GetItemByID(cartItemID, c.CartID); on pgx.ErrNoRows returns ErrCartItemNotFound → handler maps to 404 (handler_update_item.go:93-99). The qty=0 short-circuit at service.go:140-141 happens AFTER the GetItemByID call. TD endpoint `cart.remove-item` idempotency clause: "Removing an already-removed line returns current cart state — no error"; AMB-004 routes qty=0 through remove-item logic.
findings.impact: Two semantically-identical client actions (POST update-item qty=0 vs POST remove-item) produce different responses on retry. Breaks at-least-once retry safety from frontends and breaks the AMB-004 documented equivalence.
findings.recommendation: When req.qty == 0, route to removeItemInternal BEFORE the GetItemByID precheck (or treat ErrNoRows as a 200 no-op for qty=0). Simplest patch: in UpdateItem, after fetching the cart row, if qty==0 jump straight to removeItemInternal which already tolerates 0 rows deleted (service.go:220-222 only logs when rows>0).

findings.title: AddItem catalog call uses request context with no per-call deadline
findings.evidence: service.go:70 — `s.catalog.GetProductDetail(ctx, productID)` with raw request ctx. UpdateItem path (service.go:145-148) explicitly wraps a 3s timeout context. AddItem relies on the gateway-level middleware.Timeout(timeoutDuration) configured in router.go:35 plus the http client's 15s default.
findings.impact: Inconsistent timeout posture; a slow catalog backend on add-item path could occupy the request context up to the gateway timeout (typically 30s) instead of the desired ~3s budget per upstream call.
findings.recommendation: Wrap a `context.WithTimeout(ctx, fanoutCfg.TimeoutMS*ms)` around the AddItem catalog call, mirroring UpdateItem (service.go:145-146).

findings.title: Inner upstream error strings reach wrapper.Respond Err field; verify they do not surface to client body
findings.evidence: client_catalog.go:59 returns `fmt.Errorf("catalog: unexpected response code=%d envelope_code=%s", ...)`. handler_add_item.go:90-95 default branch passes Err: err to wrapper.Respond. Same pattern in handler_update_item.go and handler_read.go.
findings.impact: If wrapper.Respond serializes Err.Error() into the response payload, clients learn upstream-service identity and internal envelope codes (information disclosure / fingerprinting).
findings.recommendation: Confirm common/wrapper.Respond logs Err but does NOT echo it to JSON body. If it does, sanitize: log internally, return only generic INTERNAL_ERROR / UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT codes to the client (TD failure_codes already define this contract).

findings.title: user_id scoping is consistently enforced — PASS
findings.evidence: handler_add_item.go:38, handler_update_item.go:43, handler_read.go:37 all uuid.Parse(claims.Sub) → userID, then service methods use it as the FIRST WHERE clause filter. access/storage_cart.go GetCartByUserID, GetOrCreateByUserID, GetCartWithItems all filter `WHERE user_id = $1`. cart_items access is always WHERE cart_id IN (SELECT cart_id FROM carts WHERE user_id=$1) via the GetCartByUserID precheck. No cross-cart query path exists.

findings.title: Concurrent add-item ON CONFLICT — PASS, tx-safe
findings.evidence: access/storage_cart.go:55-65 — INSERT … ON CONFLICT (cart_id, product_id) DO UPDATE SET qty = cart.cart_items.qty + EXCLUDED.qty. Postgres takes a row-level lock on the conflicting row within the same statement; second tx blocks until first commits, then reads post-commit qty for its UPDATE. Final qty = sum of both adds, no lost update, no duplicate row. UNIQUE(cart_id, product_id) constraint enforces invariant. Two-device add-from-A + add-from-B on same SKU produces qty=A+B exactly.

findings.title: All SQL parameterized — PASS
findings.evidence: Every storage_cart.go and storage_cart_clear_idempotency.go query uses $1..$N placeholders with pgx.Tx.Exec / pool.Query. DeleteItems uses ANY($2::uuid[]) with pgx native array binding (storage_cart.go:93-100). No fmt.Sprintf-into-SQL. No string concat anywhere in app/cart/.

findings.title: No PII in logs — PASS
findings.evidence: All slog calls in app/cart/*.go log only UUIDs (user_id, cart_id, cart_item_id) or static strings. claims.Email is never read. wrapper.BindJSON receives slog.String("handler", ...) only. No request body / claims fields beyond Sub are logged.

findings.title: cart.read line shape carries available data but no explicit `reason` short-code
findings.evidence: service.go:341-353 — CartItemView has CurrentPrice, AvailableQty, ProductStatus, Checkoutable. Reviewer checklist asked for `available` flag + explicit reason. Status doubles as reason when productStatus=="CATALOG_UNREACHABLE" (service.go:336-339), which conflates a pseudo-status with the real product lifecycle states (ACTIVE/INACTIVE/DELETED).
findings.recommendation: Add a separate `reason` string field to CartItemView populated only when checkoutable=false, with values like "product_inactive", "product_deleted", "out_of_stock", "catalog_unreachable", "inventory_unreachable" (latter resolves H-2). Keep productStatus pure (the catalog enum).

findings.title: Catalog/inventory clients only check HTTP status, not envelope code
findings.evidence: client_catalog.go:58 — `if resp.Code != http.StatusOK || resp.Response.Data == nil`. resp.Code is the HTTP status; the envelope `Code` (success/error) is only used in the error message string. Same in client_inventory.go:53.
findings.recommendation: Also assert `resp.Response.Code == "SUCCESS"` (or whatever app.CodeSuccess resolves to) before trusting Data. Prevents an upstream returning HTTP 200 + envelope error from being treated as a valid response.

findings.title: remove-item is 501 while update-item(qty=0) works — minor surface inconsistency
findings.evidence: handler_remove_item.go:14-20 returns 501 NOT_IMPLEMENTED. handler_update_item.go accepts qty=0. Customers/SDKs that call remove-item will fail until M-2 fix lands and the stub is replaced.
findings.recommendation: Un-stub RemoveItem in the same PR that fixes M-2 — it's a 5-line wrapper around RemoveItem service method that already exists (service.go:192-202).

simplify_suggestions.title: Drop the unnecessary tx wrapper in persistClearIdempotencyNoTx
simplify_suggestions.evidence: service.go:421-431 — wraps a single INSERT in BeginTx/Commit/Rollback. SaveClearIdempotency could accept pool.Exec directly.
simplify_suggestions.benefit: Removes ~10 lines and one round-trip for the no-cart idempotency case.

simplify_suggestions.title: Remove dead stockMu mutex in ReadCart
simplify_suggestions.evidence: service.go:272, 309-316 — sync.Mutex protects stockMap. Only the single inventory goroutine writes; all reads happen after g.Wait() (line 320). Mutex is unreachable contention and adds noise.
simplify_suggestions.benefit: Removes mutex declaration and 4 lock/unlock calls; no behavior change.

simplify_suggestions.title: AddItem and removeItemInternal both end with full ReadCart fan-out — consider lighter return path
simplify_suggestions.evidence: service.go:116, 230 — every mutation ends with a full catalog+inventory fan-out for the response. For a 50-item cart that's 50 catalog calls per write.
simplify_suggestions.benefit: Out of L1 scope; flag for L2 — possibly cache the last-read enrichment per request, or return a lighter shape from mutations and let clients re-read on demand. Acceptable for v0.1.

checks_passed: Auth user_id == claims.sub on every endpoint (REV-L1-CART-L-1)
JWT verification wired via middleware on all 5 routes (router.go:62)
Quantity validation on add-item: min=1, max=100 (handler_add_item.go:18)
Catalog/inventory client default 15s timeout via httpclient.NewHTTPClient; cart.read fan-out 3s per call (service.go:259)
non_blocking_followups: REV-L1-CART-H-1 (clear-on-checkout claims.sub guard at un-stub time)
